supporting_observations.claim: DC-HD-01 recorded two failed network logons for ben.carter using NTLM from 192.0.2.45, with incorrect-password status, at 13:41:55 and 13:43:20 UTC.
At 13:44:45 UTC, DC-HD-01 recorded a successful Kerberos network logon for ben.carter from the same IP address, 192.0.2.45.
On WS-BCARTER-01, Explorer set ben.carter's ProxyEnable value to 0 at 13:39:30 UTC, indicating the configured proxy was disabled.
The sequence of proxy disabling followed by failed logons and then a successful logon is suspicious, but these records do not establish that the activity was malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy logs for the proxy host were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC because of a collection outage, overlapping the alerted activity.
The provided records do not identify the device or person behind source IP 192.0.2.45.
claims_not_established: Whether 192.0.2.45 maps to ben.carter's workstation, another internal device, or an external source.
Whether ben.carter performed or authorized the proxy change and authentication attempts.
Whether the successful logon was part of legitimate activity or an unauthorized session.
Whether proxy traffic occurred after the proxy setting was disabled.
additional_evidence_needed: Determine the device and network assignment for 192.0.2.45 at the relevant times, using available DHCP, address-management, or network records.
Recover proxy logs for the outage window if available, and review traffic associated with WS-BCARTER-01 and the source IP.
Review endpoint process, network, and logon-session telemetry on WS-BCARTER-01 around 13:38–13:45 UTC to establish what initiated the setting change and authentication activity.
Confirm with ben.carter whether the activity was expected.
